question_text: Stan invests £$3500$ for $33$ months at $8\%$ p.a. interest compounded quarterly. Find its maturing value.

subparts.stem: Stan invests £$3500$ for $33$ months at $8\%$ p.a. interest compounded quarterly. Find its maturing value.
subparts.solution:
$$\text{There is 1 time period every 3 months, so } n = \frac{33}{3} = 11 \text{ time periods.}$$
$$\text{Each time period the investment increases by } i = \frac{8\%}{4} = 2\%.$$
$$\therefore \text{the amount after 33 months is } u_{11} = u_0 \times (1 + i)^{11}$$
$$= 3500 \times (1.02)^{11} \quad \{2\% = 0.02\}$$
$$\approx 4351.81$$
$$\text{The maturing value of the account is } \text{£}4351.81.$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For compounding every 3 months (quarterly), divide annual interest rate by 4, and calculate periods by total months divided by 3.
step_by_step: Determine number of 3-month periods in 33 months: $n = \frac{33}{3} = 11$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing the annual rate by 12 instead of 4, or miscounting the number of quarters.
